tldr: Thinking Machines Lab released open-weight looping models for local multimodal and reasoning research, while Signal introduced partial screen protections against operating-system AI agents.

New papers tackle training smaller models, sparse attention, speech event labeling and robot safety; international discussions about autonomous weapons and AI infrastructure remain proposals or negotiations, not settled safeguards, and all author benchmark claims need replication.

news.title: Thinking Machines Lab releases Apache-licensed Inkling 2 Mini
news.summary: Inkling 2 Mini is a 26.4B-parameter sparse MoE with 3.4B active parameters and three shared-layer loops per token. It accepts text/images, emits text and provides downloadable Apache-2.0 weights.
news.why_it_matters: A published low-bit checkpoint offers developers a local alternative for coding and tool-use research, with adjustable application integrations.
news.caveat: 5.4B effective activations per token are not equivalent to 5.4B unique weights; benchmark leadership, speed and 1M context are provider claims and workload-dependent. About 20GB checkpoint and at least 32GB GPU/unified memory are recommended.

news.title: Open variable-loop model enables studies of hidden reasoning and oversight
news.summary: Thinking Machines Lab published TML-d24-varloop-research, a 26.4B total-parameter multimodal research checkpoint allowing inference-time selection of shared-middle-layer passes.
news.why_it_matters: Holding weights fixed while changing loop count provides a controlled way to compare hidden computation, reasoning performance and chain-of-thought monitorability.
news.caveat: Only a research checkpoint, not a production API. Authors trained with 1–5 passes; generalization to more passes and no-CoT safety effects are not independently validated.

news.title: Signal adds screenshot defenses against operating-system AI agents
news.summary: Signal announced screen-capture restrictions on iOS 27 and selective Android AI-assistant capture checks to limit automated reading of private conversations.
news.why_it_matters: OS-integrated agents can cross app privacy boundaries even when message transport is encrypted; Signal is testing app-level mitigations.
news.caveat: Protections are incomplete, can be disabled and do not block all filesystem or OS-level access; Signal did not report that this announcement was a newly confirmed leak.

news.title: UN weapons talks commit to more autonomous-weapons negotiations through 2028
news.summary: Countries at Geneva Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons talks agreed to continue negotiating autonomous-weapons rules within two years, Reuters reported November 21 UTC.
news.why_it_matters: Human control of lethal decisions remains an international governance issue as increasingly autonomous targeting tools proliferate.
news.caveat: No binding global ban or substantive treaty was adopted; the U.S., Russia and Israel opposed the requested binding rules, and consensus language remains limited.

news.title: US Treasury chief says Washington and Beijing backed human oversight of military AI
news.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC that Trump and Xi agreed humans should be involved in major military decisions supported by AI, Reuters reported.
news.why_it_matters: An attributed bilateral position may affect expectations for human involvement in military AI, separate from multilateral treaty negotiations.
news.caveat: This is one official's description of an agreement, not a published, independently verified, binding treaty or deployed safeguard.

news.title: US president threatens penalties for American companies building data centers abroad
news.summary: President Trump said his administration would penalize U.S. companies that build overseas data centers, suggesting a large tax; Reuters reported the remarks from a press conference.
news.why_it_matters: A future policy could materially change regional AI capacity planning, latency, and foreign investment decisions.
news.caveat: A public threat is not an enacted law, published tax rule or proof penalties have been imposed; key implementation details remain unknown.

news.title: AutoMaster paper uses skill-guided rollouts to improve post-training of small models
news.summary: AutoMaster generates behavior-focused skill instructions to shape teacher trajectories before SFT, reporting gains of 1.42–8.99 percentage points over a controlled baseline on 4B/9B coding, search and terminal tasks.
news.why_it_matters: Targets better synthetic training demonstrations rather than simply buying more teacher calls or model scale.
news.caveat: Preprint, author-selected benchmarks and no independent replication; skill instruction leakage and broader task transfer require study.

news.title: HiSA research sparsifies attention feature dimensions instead of tokens
news.summary: Hidden Sparse Attention omits selected RoPE query-key feature-product components, reporting about one-third of the dot-product terms in tested settings and FlashAttention-3 integration.
news.why_it_matters: Feature-axis sparsity offers a different computational tradeoff from token pruning or sliding-window attention.
news.caveat: Training from scratch and custom kernels limit drop-in adoption; author-measured accuracy, memory and speed have not been independently replicated.

news.title: dLoop explores more computation before diffusion-language token commitment
news.summary: The dLoop preprint adds repeated parameter-shared middle-block processing of a partially masked sequence before committing generated tokens, and reports favorable accuracy/throughput tradeoffs on selected tasks.
news.why_it_matters: Refinement loops may reduce errors in parallel token generation without only changing confidence thresholds.
news.caveat: Authors report mixed throughput comparisons depending on baseline and accounting for repeated passes; results are not a general speed guarantee.

news.title: Multi-turn safeguarding study finds risks missed when warning cues appear gradually
news.summary: A research preprint using nine scenarios and over 7,400 simulated conversations reports that several assistants met community-worker safeguarding criteria less often when subtle risk cues were dispersed across turns.
news.why_it_matters: Tests whether safety evaluations built around one obvious message overstate performance in longer, realistic conversations.
news.caveat: Scenario judgments are from three support workers; synthetic interactions, model versions and prompts constrain generalization. These are findings, not a confirmed individual-user incident.

news.title: Xing-Audio study combines speech transcripts and six classes of vocal sounds
news.summary: Authors describe a 1.7B-parameter model trained with about 800,000 cross-audited/mined utterances to label speech alongside non-verbal vocalizations such as breathing.
news.why_it_matters: Unified recognition could preserve communication cues that conventional speech-to-text systems omit.
news.caveat: Author benchmarks only; weights, inference code, dataset and evaluation artifacts are described as planned for release, not currently verified available.

news.title: AgentRoboCritic analyzes action-by-action robot-control failures
news.summary: Researchers introduce intent-grounded critiques across 12 robot-manipulation benchmarks with 12,844 labeled actions; they report a fine-tuned critic improves failure-mode accuracy in their human-annotated test.
news.why_it_matters: Action-level diagnosis can reveal grasping, alignment and recovery weaknesses hidden by episode pass rates.
news.caveat: The disclosed benchmark and fine-tuned critic do not establish safe or robust physical deployment; reported performance is from a research test, not independent field validation.

news.title: SAFI trains vision-language-action robots to halt prohibited tasks mid-execution
news.summary: State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI) trains a policy to hold a safe stationary arm and gripper state when takeover occurs after a forbidden task has already started, tested on LIBERO/BadLIBERO.
news.why_it_matters: A refusal at task start alone is insufficient when a robot is already moving or holding an object.
news.caveat: The 1.3% prohibited-completion result and lack of recorded physical incidents apply only to evaluated setups; do not infer guaranteed real-world safety.

news.title: Anytime-valid testing paper formalizes when an AI answer sampler may stop
news.summary: Researchers propose reward-weighted answer clustering and an e-process-based stopping rule that can certify sampled majority answers under stated statistical assumptions.
news.why_it_matters: Variable per-query sample budgets could cut unnecessary best-of-N inference while bounding a specific premature-certification error.
news.caveat: A certified answer majority is not a guarantee of factual correctness; sequential validity depends on distributional assumptions and the reported cost gains are author-evaluated.

technologies.name: Inkling 2 Mini
technologies.explanation: Apache-2.0 open-weight 26.4B-total/3.4B-active MoE with three shared-middle-layer passes, native text/image input, text generation and mixed NVFP4/MXFP8 weights.
technologies.conditional_advantage: A laptop or single 32GB-class device can run a comparatively capable coding/tool model without sending prompts to a hosted API; economics depend on hardware and decoding workload.
best_fit_uses: LoRA or post-training experiments using published checkpoint
tradeoffs: Repeated layer passes add inference work
Cloud alternatives may have stronger frontier reasoning
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Checkpoint approximately 20GB, typically 32GB or more GPU/unified memory (DGX Spark, capable NVIDIA card or Apple Silicon); support depends on model-specific Ollama/SGLang/vLLM integration.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Model card explicitly states Apache-2.0 for released weights; inspect third-party runtime and training dependencies separately.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Weights downloadable as of checked date; third-party hosts and runtime compatibility may vary.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: Local weights have no per-token license fee stated, but hardware/electricity and third-party hosted API/Tinker service fees may apply.

technologies.name: TML-d24-varloop-research
technologies.explanation: Open-weight 26.4B-total, 3.4B-active model exposing an inference-time loop count over shared transformer middle layers; trained across one through five passes.
technologies.conditional_advantage: Holding checkpoint weights constant while changing loop depth isolates computational-depth effects for interpretability, hidden-reasoning, and oversight studies.
tradeoffs: Research-only checkpoint, no Tinker or public model API
Memory and latency increase with extra passes
Findings are not generalizable to all transformer families
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Approximately 20GB checkpoint, 32GB+ GPU/unified memory, specialized mixed NVFP4/MXFP8 runtime; no API availability.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Published model card says Apache-2.0 weights; optional runtime dependencies separately licensed.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Research weights downloadable as of checked date; no public hosted API.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: No model license fee specified; local computing costs and any downstream hosting costs are separate.

technologies.name: Hidden Sparse Attention (HiSA)
technologies.explanation: RoPE-aware partial query-key dot products that omit statically chosen feature dimensions, with proposed FlashAttention-3 training and inference kernel integrations.
technologies.conditional_advantage: May reduce dot-product multiplication/memory costs when training models around this rule and deploying on supported GPU kernels, versus full feature-dimension attention.
best_fit_uses: Training RoPE-based decoder models from scratch
tradeoffs: Reported gains depend on retraining and kernel support
Generic pretrained-model drop-in accuracy not established
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: CUDA/GPU FlashAttention-3-style kernel integration suggested; precise architecture/kernel requirements must be confirmed in code and reproduction.
technologies.license_uncertainty: A linked code repository is described in paper; code license not audited.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Research implementation mentioned, but production packaging and binary availability not independently verified.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: No public product price; research implementation may still incur GPU retraining and integration costs.

technologies.name: AutoMaster with Skill-Guided Fine-Tuning
technologies.explanation: Agentic post-training workflow that analyzes rollout errors, generates natural-language skill constraints for a teacher and selects examples for target-model supervised fine-tuning.
technologies.conditional_advantage: May improve smaller coding/search/terminal models with the same teacher/data budget if unguided successful trajectories contain repeated bad habits.
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Requires teacher agent inference, trajectory storage, SFT training GPUs appropriate to 4B/9B target checkpoints; no plug-and-play deployed API verified.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Paper access verified; code/data/model licensing not established.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Research method described, runnable artifact not verified.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: No vendor product price; dependent on training and teacher-inference costs.

technologies.name: Xing-Audio-NVVASR
technologies.explanation: Proposed 1.7B ASR model producing speech transcripts with inline labels for six non-verbal vocalization classes from speech and breath/event-rich audio.
technologies.conditional_advantage: Could retain labeled non-speech vocal events that generic speech-to-text often drops, conditional on evaluation transfer and released artifacts.
alternatives: Whisper-like ASR plus separate event detector
Dedicated voice activity and sound event detection pipeline
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: 1.7B model; precise memory, inference latency, GPU/CPU runtime not published in verified abstract.
technologies.license_uncertainty: No model/data/code licenses verified; authors describe prospective release.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Planned model weights, inference code and benchmark releases are not verified available.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: No product pricing published; research training/inference hardware costs would apply.

terms.name: Looped transformer
terms.definition: A transformer that reuses the same layer weights over more than one sequential computation pass, increasing effective compute depth without adding a fresh parameter set per pass.
terms.mechanism: An intermediate layer block processes a token representation repeatedly, sometimes with a fixed or selectable number of passes, before the next stage or emitted token.
terms.example: Inkling 2 Mini applies its 12 middle layers three times per output token, with shared weights.
terms.caveat: Reusing weights is not free: additional passes increase latency and activations, and hidden intermediate computation may be harder to supervise than printed reasoning traces.

terms.name: Hidden-dimension sparse attention
terms.definition: An attention computation that skips selected query-key feature-dimension products rather than skipping attention links between token positions.
terms.mechanism: For RoPE queries and keys, HiSA chooses dot-product feature subsets with a fixed position-conditioned rule and computes a smaller sum for each retained token pair.
terms.example: A HiSA-trained model may calculate only about a third of the dense query-key feature products in the reported experiment.
terms.caveat: Not synonymous with token-sparse attention; accuracy depends on training/kernel details and author results do not prove universal speedups.

terms.name: Non-verbal vocalization recognition
terms.definition: Recognition and labeling of human vocal sounds other than lexical speech, such as laughter, sobbing or audible breathing, often alongside a transcript.
terms.mechanism: A speech/audio model predicts aligned event categories on acoustic segments and may insert typed tags into transcribed output.
terms.example: An ASR transcript adds [breathing] between two spoken sentences instead of omitting it.
terms.caveat: Labels are model- and dataset-specific; recognition cannot reliably infer emotion, mental state or intent from sound alone.

terms.name: State-Aware Fallback Imitation
terms.definition: A robotic imitation-learning procedure that supplies safe alternative actions for prohibited behavior at intermediate task states, not only a refusal at initiation.
terms.mechanism: Fallback trajectories assign stationary manipulator commands and consistent gripper targets, then joint policy adaptation trains to enact them while preserving permitted tasks.
terms.example: If a robot discovers a disallowed task while holding an object, its learned response keeps the gripper stable rather than releasing the object abruptly.
terms.caveat: An experimentally learned fallback does not establish safe physical execution across unseen robots, hazards or state distributions.

terms.name: Anytime-valid answer certification
terms.definition: A sequential test that lets a sampler stop at a data-dependent time while maintaining a specified bound on the chance of incorrectly certifying a property under the test's assumptions.
terms.mechanism: A nonnegative e-process accumulates betting evidence across sampled answers; crossing a preset threshold can certify a majority-cluster property without ordinary repeated-peeking inflation.
terms.example: For repeated model answers, stop drawing candidates once an e-process supports that an answer dominates the model's own sampling distribution at the chosen error tolerance.
terms.caveat: Certifying statistical dominance does not prove the answer true; validity needs the assumed sequential sampling/model conditions.
